Jwt.//: LOCAL DEVELOPMENT ONLY. Production must supply Auth__Jwt__SigningKey as an environment variable.

Security.//: LOCAL DEVELOPMENT ONLY. Production must supply Auth__Security__HashingKey as an environment variable.

Otp.//: Development only. Production keeps the 60s cooldown from appsettings.json. Waiting a minute between a registration and a sign-in is friction with no security value on a host that writes the codes to its own log, and it would make the browser tests spend most of their time asleep.

RateLimits.//: Development only. Production keeps the defaults in code (5 requests and 10 verifications per 15 minutes per address). The browser tests register and sign in many times from one address, and would otherwise be throttled by a control aimed at the public internet.
RateLimits.//Windows: Development only. Every default lives in code and is the production number; these raise the per-address windows that a browser suite trips purely by running many journeys from one machine — page loads, listings, uploads, store applications and reports. Production configures none of this.

//Listings: Development only. B-1's 10-per-category-per-month default lives in code and is the production number. Raised here for the same reason as the rate limits above: the browser suite creates far more than 10 listings a month from one seller while exercising unrelated flows, and quota enforcement is not what those tests are about.
//Payments: Development only. Points success/error redirects at the local Vite dev server. Epoint credentials stay unset here on purpose — Development always uses the simulated gateway (DevelopmentPaymentGatewayClient) regardless of what this section holds.
//AllowedHosts: Local work and the integration test host talk to Kestrel by whatever name they like.
//Serilog: Development keeps the human-readable console template. Production writes structured JSON instead (see appsettings.json) — this array entry overrides that formatter back to the default so a WriteTo array specified in the base file does not leak an unreadable format into local work.
